biography:
Graham Mann is a British singer/songwriter and multi-instrumentalist best known as a long-time collaborator of the renowned artist Matt Berry. Mann has worked closely with Berry on numerous projects, including the 2026 album Everything’s Peachy, released under the Matt Berry Trio, where he joined Berry and fellow collaborator Phill Scragg. His musical contributions span piano, trombone, and other instruments, and he has been credited on several of Berry’s works, including Are You Being Served, London Weekend Television, and Open University.

As a singer/songwriter, Mann brings a distinctive voice to the collaborative jazz, modern classical, and electronic soundscapes that define the Matt Berry Trio’s output. His partnership with Berry reflects a deep artistic synergy, with Mann often serving as a key creative force in shaping the trio’s leftward musical turn away from traditional songwriting toward more experimental and instrumental compositions. Mann’s versatility and musical depth have made him an integral part of Berry’s evolving artistic journey, particularly in the trio’s exploration of jazz and electronic influences.

While Mann’s solo work remains less documented in public sources, his significance within the broader context of Matt Berry’s musical universe is well established. His role as a trusted collaborator underscores his reputation as a skilled and adaptable musician who enhances the sonic richness of Berry’s projects. Through his work with the Matt Berry Trio and other collaborations, Graham Mann continues to contribute meaningfully to the contemporary landscape of British singer/songwriter and experimental music.
